summary: Full Riftbound test pass: headless tracer invariants + monkey gameplay-flow + per-card playtest on N untested cards. Returns one merged report.

invariants.sample: engine has 1 exhausted board cards, DOM shows 0

findings.what: Petal Pixie (unl-076-219) sitting alone in player-1's base displays an 'Effective Might' badge of 3 (printed Might 2) in both the BEFORE and AFTER screenshots. No unit with [Temporary] exists anywhere, and Petal Pixie is not at a battlefield, so its Might should be 2. Root cause: the rules-text parser turns 'I have +1 [Might] for each of your units with [Temporary] at my battlefield' into a static modify-might with amount:1 and an opaque `per` string; applyStaticEffect in static-abilities.ts ignores `per` and applies a flat +1 staticMightBonus every recalculation.
findings.why_wrong: Petal Pixie's text grants +1 Might only per friendly [Temporary] unit at its battlefield; with zero such units (and while at base) the bonus is +0. The engine is granting an unconditional +1, which will also miscompute combat/showdown Might totals, not just the badge.
findings.reason: Ran parseAbilities on Petal Pixie's rulesText: output is {type:"modify-might", amount:1, per:"of your units with [Temporary] at my battlefield", target:"self"} — static-parser.ts:648-681 falls through to the flat `amount` + opaque `per` branch because parseForEachQualifier (static-parser.ts:36-60) only recognizes two qualifiers. Engine applyStaticEffect (packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/static-abilities.ts:566-570, 630-635) treats numeric amount as a flat bonus and never reads `per`; getAllBoardCards (line 58) includes base cards so it applies in base too. Card unl/petal-pixie.ts has no explicit abilities so enrich-cards.ts uses the parser. Screenshot 25.png shows the "3" badge on Petal Pixie alone in base.

findings.what: Player clicked 'Recycle Rune -> Order Rune (ready)'. In the AFTER state the Order Rune was only exhausted (+1 energy, 1->2) but was still in the rune zone (runeCount 2, rune deck still 10) and no Order power was added (power {}); recycleRune for that rune is still listed in available moves. The actual recycle only landed later (visible by step 4: power.order=1, rune gone). The UI implements panel-recycle of a ready rune as two separate dispatches (exhaustRune, then a client-side 100ms poll loop up to 10 tries to send recycleRune — apps/riftbound-app/public/js/gameplay/interactions.js quickRecycleRune), so the player sees an intermediate 'tapped but not recycled' board and, if the poll window (1s) is missed, the click silently degrades to a plain exhaust with no recycle/power.
findings.why_wrong: A single 'Recycle' action should resolve as one action: rune goes to the bottom of the rune deck (rule 594) and its Recycle ability adds 1 power of its domain. DESIGN.md says recycling a ready rune auto-taps then recycles as one gesture; exposing a state where energy was gained but the rune is neither recycled nor power added misrepresents the result of the action the player chose, and the timeout path can drop the recycle entirely.
findings.ruleOrCard: 594 (Recycle) / basic rune Recycle: Add [power]; DESIGN.md rune auto-tap+recycle
findings.reason: Source matches the claim exactly. The action panel's 'Recycle Rune -> <rune> (ready)' sub-item is wired to quickRecycleRune (apps/riftbound-app/public/js/gameplay/render/actions.js:363-368: `splitByState && !isExh(m) ... ? \`quickRecycleRune(${JSON.stringify(m.params?.runeId)}, this)\``). quickRecycleRune (apps/riftbound-app/public/js/gameplay/interactions.js:427-456) dispatches executeMove(exhaustMove) first (line 441), then runs a client-side poll `tryRecycle` that re-checks findCard(runeId).meta.exhausted and sends recycleRune only once seen, retrying `if (++tries <= 10) setTimeout(tryRecycle, 100)` (line 454) — i.e. two separate dispatches with a ~1s window after which the recycle is silently abandoned. Trace corroborates: step 3 (click-sub 'Order Rune (ready)') shows energy 1->2, Order Rune exhausted but still in runePool, power {}, recycleRune for that rune still in moves; step 4 shows power.order=1 and the rune gone, so the recycle landed as a later separate frame.

findings.what: Step 4: player clicked 'Play Unit — Petal Pixie to base' with 2 energy available (cost 2). In the AFTER state/screenshot nothing about the play is reflected: Petal Pixie still in hand, base empty, energy still 2, no toast/rejection, no in-flight indicator. The only visible change is the tail of the PREVIOUS action (quickRecycleRune's deferred recycle of the Order Rune landing: rune gone, +1 Order, rune deck 10→11). The Pixie play only shows up one step later (step 5: Pixie in base, exhausted, energy 2→0 — all correct per rule 143.4 and cost).
findings.why_wrong: Not a rules violation — the engine result, once it landed, is correct (cost fully paid, unit entered exhausted and is rendered rotated, resource bar matches runePools). The defect is responsiveness: a legal playUnit on a local server took >~0.5s to round-trip (server executes move + rebuilds available moves for both seats synchronously before replying) and the UI gives no pending/in-flight feedback, so to a human the click looks ignored and invites a double-click. Same one-step lag is visible for recycleRune at steps 3→4 and 14→15. Flagging as low severity latency/feedback only; no mandatory prompt was skipped, no underpayment, no missed trigger.
findings.reason: Trace verified: step 03→04→05 shows exactly the described one-step lag (04: energy 2, power.order 0→1, runePool 2→1, base [], Pixie still in hand; 05: base=[Petal Pixie], energy 0, hand 9→8). Screenshot mtimes (03=33.565s, 04=34.095s, 05=34.625s) with the harness's fixed `waitForTimeout(400)` (monkey-drive.ts:280) mean the playUnit round-trip exceeded ~400ms on localhost. Source confirms both halves of the mechanism: (1) UI: the action-panel Play Unit button calls executeMove directly (render/actions.js:341-342), and executeMove is pure fire-and-forget `ws.send({type:"move"...})` with no pending state, button disable, or optimistic render (game-flow.js:25-26); the only in-flight guard, `window.__rbTurnActionInFlight`, is a non-visual space/end-turn double-press latch (init.js:31-40, hotkeys.js:266-268) and is not set for panel plays. (2) Server: gameWsMessage runs executeMove → buildGameSnapshot → buildAvailableMoves(actor) synchronously before ws.send(move_accepted) (server/ws-game.ts:90-161), then keeps blocking the single event loop with buildAvailableMoves+snapshot per other client (163-178) and sandbox goldfish auto-play (181+), so the next queued move (Pixie) cannot start until the prior recycleRune's tail work finishes. Step 03's 'Order Rune (ready)' indeed routes through quickRecycleRune (render/actions.js:366-368 → interactions.js:427-455, deferred recycle via 100ms setTimeout poll), matching the 'tail of previous action' description. Minor nit: actor reply is sent before other-seat enumeration, not after, but the effective latency claim holds because of event-loop serialization. Low-severity responsiveness/feedback finding, not a rules violation, as the claim itself states.

findings.what: Step 5 clicked the still-rendered 'Play Unit — Soaring Scout to base' button, but the result was Petal Pixie (from the step-4 click) landing in base and energy 2→0; the Soaring Scout play was then sent anyway and bounced by the server a step later with an opaque toast 'Move rejected: Move 'playUnit' condition not met' (visible only in 06.png). The action panel kept advertising both 2-cost plays at 'Energy 2' for >400ms after the first play was submitted, with no in-flight disable, so the player's second click targeted a move that was already unaffordable.

The defect is UI: available-action buttons are not invalidated/disabled while a move is in flight (only the Space hotkey has __rbTurnActionInFlight), so a stale, no-longer-legal move is offered and clickable, and the rejection message does not say 'not enough energy (0/2)'. A human sees 'I clicked Soaring Scout, Petal Pixie appeared, then an unexplained error'.
findings.ruleOrCard: Soaring Scout (ogn-216-298) / Petal Pixie (unl-076-219); cost payment rule 356 (can't play without paying full cost)
findings.reason: Trace matches: step 04 snapshot (taken after the Petal Pixie click) still lists both playUnit moves at energy 2 with empty base; step 05 (click Soaring Scout) yields base=[Petal Pixie], energy 0; 06.png shows toast "Move rejected: Move 'playUnit' condition not met" (text from packages/core/src/engine/rule-engine.ts:833, surfaced verbatim by websocket.js:148 showToast(`Move rejected: ${msg.error}`)). Source confirms no in-flight guard on action buttons: render/actions.js:340-345 renders playUnit buttons with onclick='executeMove(...)' directly, and executeMove (game-flow.js:3-27) just ws.send()s with no disable/in-flight state. The only in-flight latch, window.__rbTurnActionInFlight, is checked/set solely in init.js:31-40 (Space key) and hotkeys.js:266-268, and cleared in websocket.js:94/123/138 — never consulted by action-panel clicks. Engine behavior is rules-correct; defect is UI staleness + opaque rejection message.

findings.what: Step 6 was a drag of the exhausted Petal Pixie from base toward a battlefield. The engine correctly offered no standardMove (unit is exhausted) so the drag was a no-op and state is unchanged — that part is correct. However the AFTER screenshot shows a toast "Move rejected: Move 'playUnit' condition not met". This is the late-arriving server rejection of step 5's 'Play Unit Soaring Scout to base' click (cost 2, energy was already 0 after Petal Pixie resolved). The UI (a) let the player click a Play Unit action button built from stale availableMoves that the engine then refused, and (b) surfaced the raw engine condition string instead of a player-facing reason (e.g. 'Not enough energy (0/2) to play Soaring Scout'), and it appears visually attached to an unrelated drag action.
findings.why_wrong: A player should never be offered an unaffordable play as a clickable action and then be told only "condition not met"; cost affordability (rule 143/cost payment — Soaring Scout cost 2 vs energy 0) should gate the button client-side or the rejection should name the unmet cost. Raw moveId/condition text is developer-speak, and because it rendered ~1 step late it misattributes the error to the base-unit drag.
findings.reason: Trace confirms sequence: step 4 snapshot (after clicking Play Petal Pixie) still shows energy 2 and both playUnit moves (stale, pre-move_accepted); step 5 clicked the still-rendered "Play Unit Soaring Scout to base" button; step 5 snapshot shows energy 0, no playUnit in moves; 06.png shows toast "Move rejected: Move 'playUnit' condition not met" (05.png has no toast). Drag in step 6 cannot emit playUnit (drag-drop.js:86-97 only matches standardMove for base), so the toast is step 5's rejection. Source: websocket.js:148 `showToast(`Move rejected: ${msg.error}`)` passes the raw engine string through verbatim; the string originates at packages/core/src/engine/rule-engine.ts:833 (`Move '${moveId}' condition not met`, emitted whenever a condition returns bare `false`), and playUnit's condition returns plain boolean from canAffordCard (play-unit.ts:451ff) with no ConditionFailure reason, so an unaffordable play can never produce a player-facing "not enough energy" message. Sidebar action buttons (render/actions.js:431-441) call executeMove directly from availableMoves with no in-flight guard, so a second click before move_accepted arrives sends a stale move. Server ws-game.ts:103-108 forwards error unchanged.

findings.what: Step 27's action itself (exhaust Mind Rune) behaved correctly: energy 0->1, rune shown rotated, resource bar 'Energy 1 Runes 1/2' matches runePools, legend ability and Retreat correctly became playable. However, in the AFTER screenshot Petal Pixie (unl-076-219) sitting alone in base displays an 'Effective Might' badge of 3 (base 2). The UI badge is base + meta.staticMightBonus etc., so the engine is carrying staticMightBonus=+1 on it. Root cause: the rulesText parser turns 'I have +1 [Might] for each of your units with [Temporary] at my battlefield' into {type:'modify-might', amount:1, per:'of your units with [Temporary] at my battlefield'} and applyStaticEffect in static-abilities.ts treats numeric `amount` as a flat +1, ignoring the unparsed `per` string. This has been present since the unit was played (visible in 05.png) and persists here.
findings.why_wrong: Petal Pixie's text grants +1 Might only per friendly [Temporary] unit at its battlefield; it is at base with zero Temporary units anywhere, so its Might must be 2, not 3. The engine/parser is applying an unconditional +1, which would also make it win combats/showdowns it should lose.
findings.ruleOrCard: unl-076-219 Petal Pixie (static 'for each' Might parsed as flat +1)
findings.reason: Parser: packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/parsers/static-parser.ts:647-681 matches "I have +N :rb_might: for each QUALIFIER"; parseForEachQualifier (lines 36-60) only recognizes two qualifiers (ven-097 "other units here with my name", ven-182 "token units you control"), so "of your units with [Temporary] at my battlefield" falls through to the fallback at line 669-681 emitting {type:'modify-might', amount:1, per:'of your units with [Temporary] at my battlefield', target:'self'} (verified by running parseAbilities on the card text). Engine: packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/static-abilities.ts:566-570 in applyStaticEffect treats `typeof rawAmount === "number"` as a flat amount and never reads `effect.per` (no reference to `per` anywhere in the engine abilities dir), then line 630-636 writes staticMightBonus += 1. UI badge at apps/riftbound-app/public/js/gameplay/render/card.js:220 sums base + staticMightBonus. Reproduced with harness: Petal Pixie (unl-076-219) alone at base with no Temporary units -> state shows staticMightBonus:1, might:3 (expected 2).

findings.what: With a non-combat Showdown open at Abandoned Hall (player-1 has Focus, no chain), the engine still offers activateAbility for the legend Herald of the Arcane ('[1], [Exhaust]: Play a 1 Might Recruit unit token') and the UI shows the 'Activate Ability — Herald of the Arcane' button.
findings.why_wrong: In a Showdown Open state only Action/Reaction-timed cards and abilities are legally timed (rules 347.1, 338.1.a, 806.1.b/c.2; cf. 145.2/151.2 'not during a Showdown'). Herald of the Arcane's activated ability has no [Action] or [Reaction] tag, so it must not be activatable until the showdown ends.
findings.reason: Trace step 29: showdown active (isCombatShowdown:false, focusPlayer player-1, chain null) and `moves` includes activateAbility for player-1-legend-ogn-265-298; DOM actionButtons includes 'Activate Ability Herald of the Arcane'. Source: activate-ability.ts:39-50 `abilityTimingClass` returns "action" for any untagged activated ability whose host is not gear (line 49: `getCardType(hostCardId) === "gear" ? "standard" : "action"`), and chain-state.ts:207-208 `isLegalTiming("action")` returns true for "showdown-open". Both the move condition (line 514-515) and the enumerator (858-862) use this helper. Herald's ability (herald-of-the-arcane.ts:16-25) has no keyword/timing, so it is classified "action" and offered during Showdown. Rules contradict this: 310.1.a (abilities activated by default only in Neutral Open), 313.1.a example ("A player with Focus may not ... activate abilities that don't have the Action or Reaction keywords"), 806.1.c.2 (Action is what grants showdown activation). Only gear got the "standard" fix; legends/units still default to action timing.

findings.what: During the open Showdown at Abandoned Hall (showdown.active=true, no chain), the legal move list and the action panel offer 'Activate Ability — Herald of the Arcane' ([1], [Exhaust]: Play a Recruit token), an activated ability with no [Action]/[Reaction] tag.
findings.why_wrong: Rule 310.1.a: by default abilities can be activated only in a Neutral Open state; rule 347.1 only lets the Focus player play a card/ability that is 'legally timed' (Action or Reaction, 338.1.a.2). Herald of the Arcane's ability has neither tag, so it must not be activatable while a Showdown is in progress. The engine's move enumerator is treating Showdown Open as sufficient for untagged activated abilities.
findings.reason: abilityTimingClass() (activate-ability.ts:39-50) returns "standard" only when the host card is gear; for every other host type (Herald of the Arcane is a legend) an untagged activated ability falls through to `"action"` at line 49. The condition at line 514-515 then calls isLegalTiming("action", turnState), which (chain/chain-state.ts:198-208) returns true for "showdown-open". So an untagged legend/unit activated ability is offered during a Showdown Open state, contrary to rule 310.1.a / 145.2 / 347.1+338.1.a.2 and the rules text "Only cards and abilities with the Action or Reaction keywords can be played or activated in a Showdown State". Trace step 30 confirms: showdown.active=true, chain=null, moves include activateAbility{cardId: player-1-legend-ogn-265-298, abilityIndex:0} and the card def (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/herald-of-the-arcane.ts) has no keyword/timing on the ability.

findings.what: After the rune exhaust (energy now 2), the engine offers `activateAbility` for the legend Herald of the Arcane ('[1], [Exhaust]: Play a 1 Might Recruit unit token') and the UI shows an 'Activate Ability - Herald of the Arcane' button, while a Showdown is open at Abandoned Hall with player-1 holding Focus.

Herald of the Arcane's ability has neither keyword (unlike the rune's '[E]: [Reaction] - Add [1]', 164.2.a, which was correctly allowed). The legend ability should only be offered in Neutral Open State on the controller's turn, not mid-showdown.
findings.reason: Trace step 30/31 shows showdown active at player-1-bf-unl-205-219 with focusPlayer=player-1, chain null (showdown-open), and moves includes activateAbility for player-1-legend-ogn-265-298; DOM shows 'Activate Ability Herald of the Arcane'. findings.what: During a Showdown State (showdown active at Abandoned Hall, no chain, player-1 has Focus) the engine offered `activateAbility` for the legend Herald of the Arcane in step 31's legal moves, and in step 32 accepted it: energy 2->1, legend exhausted, and a create-token ability item was placed on the chain.
findings.why_wrong: Herald of the Arcane's ability is "[1], [Exhaust]: Play a 1 [Might] Recruit unit token." -- it has no [Action] or [Reaction] keyword. Rule 308.1.a: only cards and abilities with Action or Reaction can be played or activated in a Showdown State; 343.1.b: card abilities by default cannot be played during a Showdown State; 347.1/338.1.a.2: the Focus player may only play a *legally timed* card/ability. The move should not have been enumerated or accepted until the showdown ended and the turn returned to Neutral Open.
findings.reason: Trace step 31 (showdownStack active, chain null, focusPlayer player-1) lists activateAbility for player-1-legend-ogn-265-298; step 32 shows energy 2->1 and a create-token ability item on the chain. Herald of the Arcane (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/herald-of-the-arcane.ts:16-25) declares the ability with no keyword/timing. In packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/chain/activate-ability.ts:49, abilityTimingClass returns "action" for any non-gear activated ability lacking an Action/Reaction keyword (`getCardType(hostCardId) === "gear" ? "standard" : "action"`), and chain/chain-state.ts:208 makes "action" legal in showdown-open. So the condition at activate-ability.ts:514-516 passes during a Showdown Open State. Rules 308.1.a ("Only cards and abilities with the Action or Reaction keywords can be played or activated in a Showdown State") and 343.1.b ("Card abilities, by default, cannot be played during a Showdown State") require default (keywordless) activated abilities to be neutral-open only; the engine's non-gear default of "action" violates this.

findings.what: After player-1 clicked Pass, the engine correctly moved chain priority to player-2 (activePlayer=player-2, passedPlayers=[player-1]) and the modal shows 'Goldfish has Priority — waiting...', but the engine's legal `moves` for player-1 still include playSpell (Retreat targeting Petal Pixie) and recycleRune x2, and the UI sidebar still renders 'Play Spell Retreat' and 'Recycle Rune (2 available)' as clickable actions.
findings.why_wrong: Rule 312.1/312.1.a-b: Priority is the exclusive right to take Discretionary Actions; a player without Priority cannot play cards. Rule 338.1.b.1/339.2: passing hands Priority to the next player in turn order. Player-1 no longer holds Priority, so offering them a Reaction spell (and rune recycles outside any cost-payment window, 429.3) is illegal move enumeration.
findings.reason: Trace step 33 confirms chain.activePlayer=player-2, passedPlayers=[player-1], yet player-1's moves include playSpell(Retreat) and recycleRune x2 (passChainPriority correctly dropped). Source: play-spell.ts condition (lines 389-408) and enumerator (lines 716-726) gate only on isLegalTiming (reaction => always true, chain-state.ts:198-201), neutral-open turn-player, and showdown-open focus; there is no closed-state check that interaction.chain.activePlayer === playerId. Contrast play-unit.ts:112-115 holdsChainPriority, and resolve.ts:728/737 which gate passChainPriority on chain.activePlayer. recycleRune (resources.ts:142-196) has no priority/chain gating at all ("Players can recycle runes at any time"). Rule 312.1: Priority is the exclusive right to take Discretionary Actions; 338.1.b.1 passing hands it to next player — so enumerating a Reaction spell for player-1 after they passed is illegal.

findings.what: Petal Pixie's static '+1 Might for each of your units with [Temporary] at my battlefield' is applied as a flat, unconditional +1 Might instead of counting Temporary units at its battlefield.
findings.expected: Might = 2 + (number of friendly units with [Temporary] at Pixie's battlefield): 2 when alone in base; 3 with Keeper of Masks (Temporary) at same battlefield; 4 after a Sprite token with Temporary keyword was also created there.
findings.observed: meta.staticMightBonus is always 1 and UI 'Effective Might' shows 3 in every case: alone in base with zero Temporary units anywhere (should be 2), with 1 Temporary unit at its battlefield (3, coincidentally correct), and with 2 Temporary units (Keeper of Masks + Sprite token w/ keywords:['Temporary']) at its battlefield (should be 4). Root cause: card file has no abilities; text parser emits {type:'static', effect:{type:'modify-might', amount:1, per:'of your units with [Temporary] at my battlefield', target:'self'}} — the 'per' clause is left as an unparsed string and static-abilities.ts treats numeric amount:1 as a constant.
findings.reason: Card file /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/petal-pixie.ts:4-15 has no `abilities`, so enrich-cards.ts:30 parses rulesText. Running the parser yields {type:'static', effect:{type:'modify-might', amount:1, per:'of your units with [Temporary] at my battlefield', target:'self'}} — static-parser.ts:36-60 parseForEachQualifier only recognizes 'other unit here with my name' and 'token unit you control', so it falls through to the `per` string branch at static-parser.ts:717-729. In the engine, static-abilities.ts:628-632 applyStaticEffect treats numeric `amount` as a constant (amount = rawAmount) and there is no handling of `effect.per` anywhere in static-abilities.ts, so staticMightBonus is always +1 regardless of Temporary unit count.

findings.what: "Recycle 3 from your trash" cost: player is never asked which 3 cards to recycle when the trash holds more than 3.
findings.expected: Rule 416.5 (Garbage Grabber is the literal example): the controller chooses 3 cards from their trash to pay the cost. Expected a picker/pendingChoice (or enumerated activateAbility variants carrying recycleIds) when trash > 3.
findings.observed: With 4 cards in trash, both the enumerated activateAbility move ({abilityIndex,cardId,playerId} only, no recycleIds) and the UI 'Activate Ability' button immediately paid the cost by auto-recycling the 3 oldest trash cards (ids main-11, main-28, main-14), leaving the newest (main-19) behind; no prompt, pendingChoice stayed null. Engine's activate-ability.ts accepts an optional params.recycleIds and falls back to eligible.slice(0,N), but nothing in the server move enumeration or UI ever supplies it.
findings.reason: Engine enumerator (activate-ability.ts:1082-1095) only gates on trash count >= N for a recycle cost and never fans out recycleIds variants (result shape at 1177-1216 carries sacrificeId/discardId/targets only). Reducer (activate-ability.ts:1352-1356) uses params.recycleIds if supplied else `eligible.slice(0, recycleSpec.amount)` and moves them immediately with no pendingChoice. UI (interactions.js:459-499, executeInteractionMove on enumerated activateAbility moves) and server never construct recycleIds (grep finds it only in engine + types/moves.ts:440). So with trash > 3 the controller cannot choose which 3 to recycle, contrary to rule 416.5's Garbage Grabber example ("its controller chooses 3 cards from their trash").

findings.what: Cards recycled to pay the cost are placed on the bottom of the Main Deck in deterministic (trash) order rather than random order.
findings.expected: Rule 416.5: 'If 2 or more cards are Recycled to the Main Deck simultaneously, they are placed on the bottom of that deck in a random order.'
findings.observed: In 3 of 3 activations the 3 recycled cards appeared as the last 3 entries of mainDeck in exactly their trash order (e.g. trash [16,35,9] -> deck bottom [...,16,35,9]; trash [22,3,20,11] -> [...,22,3,20]; trash [11,28,14,19] -> [...,11,28,14]).
findings.reason: activate-ability.ts:1357-1363 pays the "Recycle N from your trash" cost with a plain for-loop that moveCard()s each chosen id to position "bottom" of mainDeck in list order (trash order / recycleIds order) with no shuffle or randomization. Rule 416.5 (whose own example is Garbage Grabber) requires the simultaneously recycled cards to be placed on the bottom in a random order.

findings.what: Play restriction 'I can't be played on your first, second, or third turns' is not enforced
findings.expected: On player-1's first turn (turn 1, turnsTaken=1) playUnit for Ol' Poro should not be offered / should be rejected
findings.observed: On turn 1 main phase `pw moves` listed playUnit for player-1-main-999-ven-029-166 and executing it succeeded: energy 6->4, Ol' Poro (might 4) entered base. Set data ven.json shows parseSuccess:false, abilities:[] for this card, so no restriction exists in the definition.
findings.reason: ven.json:1145-1163 defines ven-029-166 (Ol' Poro) with rulesText "I can't be played on your first, second, or third turns." but abilities:[] and parseSuccess:false, so no restriction exists in the card definition. The engine's play gate (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/play-restrictions.ts:69 playIsForbidden) only enforces static restrict-play abilities pulled from the registry; with an empty abilities array nothing forbids the play, and there is no turnsTaken-based self play restriction anywhere in the engine (turnsTaken is only consulted in scoring-rules.ts and a static-abilities condition). playUnit is therefore offered and succeeds on turn 1.

findings.what: Repeat cost cannot be paid through the UI for this targeted spell
findings.expected: After choosing Upstage Comedy (hand click or sidebar 'Play Spell'), the player should be offered the optional [Repeat][2] additional cost (rule 820) before/while picking targets
findings.observed: Hand click and sidebar 'Play Spell' both go straight into target mode; clicking a target immediately executes the base variant (energy 15->13, chain item has a single 'ready' effect). interactions.js pickTargetedMove/exactTargetVariant deliberately prefer !repeatCount variants and no play-cost modal is opened for targeted spells, so the repeatCount:1 variants the server enumerates are unreachable from the UI
findings.reason: Engine does enumerate Repeat variants for Upstage Comedy (play-spell.ts:1550-1583 pushes {...base, repeatCount:n} per target, plus {repeatCount:1, targets:[first,alt]} pairs), and server/snapshot.ts:19-23 forwards all of them unfiltered. On target click, pickTargetedMove (interactions.js:213-218) returns matches.find(!paidAdditionalCost && targets.length===1) — base variant is enumerated first so it wins over the repeatCount:1 same-target variant; exactTargetVariant (:241-247) explicitly prefers isBaseCostVariant (:228-230, `!repeatCount`). openPlayCostModal (render/modals.js:200-203) only handles playUnit/playFromChampionZone, so no modal path exists for playSpell. findings.what: Destination choice after banish does not offer 'any battlefield' and wrongly offers Base
findings.expected: After banishing the friendly unit, its owner plays it to ANY battlefield (both battlefields selectable; base is not a legal destination), ignoring cost.
findings.observed: choose-destination pendingChoice options were ["base"] only when no friendly units were at either battlefield (unit was forced back to base); in a second test with a friendly unit at bf2 the options were ["base","battlefield-player-2-bf-ogn-277-298"] — the empty battlefield was never offered and Base was always offered. Engine appears to apply normal play-location legality instead of the card's 'any battlefield' override.
findings.reason: Card def (riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/thrill-of-the-hunt.ts:24-27) emits play with `toLocation: { battlefield: "any" }`, but the engine never inspects that shape (no `battlefield === "any"` handling anywhere in riftbound-engine/src). In abilities/effects/play.ts:207 any non-"base" toLocation collapses to `dest = "choose"`, queuing a generic `{to:"choose", type:"move"}` chain item. That resolves in abilities/effects/move.ts:564-582, where for a card entering play from off-board (banishment) `enteringPlay` is true and options = ["base", ...battlefields filtered to bf.controller === ctx.playerId]. So Base is always offered and uncontrolled/empty battlefields are dropped — exactly the observed ["base"] / ["base","battlefield-...bf2"]. Rule 355.2.b says an effect can make otherwise-invalid locations valid; the card's "any battlefield" override is not implemented.

findings.what: Fae Porter's move trigger lets the chosen unit be moved to ANY battlefield instead of the same battlefield Fae Porter moved to.
findings.expected: After paying [chaos] and choosing a friendly unit, that unit moves to battlefield-player-1-bf-ogn-276-298 (Aspirant's Climb, where Fae Porter just moved) with no destination choice.
findings.observed: Effect is encoded as {type:'move', to:'choose'}; after picking Overzealous Fan a 'choose-destination' pendingChoice offered both battlefields (Aspirant's Climb AND Altar to Unity). Picking Altar to Unity was accepted and Overzealous Fan ended up at battlefield-player-2-bf-ogn-275-298 while Fae Porter sat at battlefield-player-1-bf-ogn-276-298. pendingChoice even carried triggerToZone=battlefield-player-1-bf-ogn-276-298 but it was not enforced.
findings.reason: Fae Porter (packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/fae-porter.ts) has no hand-authored abilities, so enrich-cards.ts parses rulesText at load. Running parseAbilities on its text yields effect {type:'move', target:{type:'unit',controller:'friendly'}, to:'choose'}. Root cause in packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-move.ts:243-266 (flexMoveMatch): the regex ends with a mandatory `(?:\s+.*)$`, so for "Move a unit you control to the same battlefield." the optional `to` group backtracks to empty and " to the same battlefield." is swallowed by the trailing clause — toStr is undefined and line 265 emits to:'choose' (verified: match groups = ["a",null,"unit",null]). Even if captured, parseLocationString (parser/impl/targets.ts:112-135) has no case for "the same battlefield" and would fall through to "base"; nothing maps it to the engine's `to:'same'`. The engine does support the correct semantics — abilities/effects/move.ts:647-651 uses ctx.triggerToZone when dest === 'same' — but with dest === 'choose' it takes move.ts:564-598, offering base + every battlefield as a choose-destination prompt, matching the observed behavior (unit could be sent to Altar to Unity instead of Aspirant's Climb).

findings.what: Starhound's on-play trigger does not return a Poro from trash to hand.
findings.expected: With Daring Poro (ogn-210-298, tags:['Poro'] in registry) in player-1's trash, resolving the 'When you play me' trigger should move Daring Poro from trash to hand (or prompt to choose it).
findings.observed: Trigger chain-2 resolved with no pendingChoice and no zone change: trash still ['player-1-main-999-ogn-210-298','player-1-main-22-ogn-016-298'], hand unchanged, no log line. Effect target is {location:'trash',type:'unit',filter:[{tag:'Bird'},{tag:'Cat'},{tag:'Dog'},{tag:'Poro'}]} and target-resolver.ts applies filter arrays with filters.every(...) (AND), so a card would need all four tags — the 'Bird, Cat, Dog, OR Poro' disjunction is lost.
findings.reason: Parser (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-return.ts:159-166) emits the tag list "Bird, Cat, Dog, or Poro" as filter: [{tag:'Bird'},{tag:'Cat'},{tag:'Dog'},{tag:'Poro'}] (confirmed by return-hand.test.ts:114-130). target-resolver.ts:357-359 applies `filters.every((f) => matchesFilter(id, f, ctx))`, and matchesFilter's tag branch (target-resolver.ts:~741) returns tags.includes(filter.tag) — so a candidate must carry all four tags. Daring Poro has tags:['Poro'] only (daring-poro.ts:15), so it fails the AND and the target set is empty; the disjunction is lost exactly as reported.

findings.what: Kinkou Initiate's play trigger draws unconditionally; the 'if your other units have total Might 5 or more' condition is not checked.
findings.expected: Played to base with zero other friendly units on the board (other-unit total Might = 0): trigger should resolve with no draw (hand stays 5, deck stays 35).
findings.observed: Trigger went on chain as {"amount":1,"type":"draw"} (no condition) and on resolution drew 1 (hand 5->6 'Void Hatchling', p1 deck 35->34).
findings.reason: Card def (packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/kinkou-initiate.ts) has no hand-authored abilities, so enrich-cards.ts:30 parses rulesText. Verified via bun: parser emits a triggered play-self ability with effect {type:"draw",amount:1} and ability-level condition {type:"total-might-at-least",amount:5,scope:"other-units"} (condition-parser.ts:782-791). The engine never evaluates that condition type: `grep -r total-might-at-least` hits only the parser; evaluateTriggerCondition in packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-runner.ts:289-521 has no branch for it and falls through to `return true` at trigger-runner.ts:520 ("Unknown condition shapes are permissive"). findings.what: [Reaction] [Exhaust]: [Add] ability is placed on the chain and waits for priority passes instead of resolving immediately
findings.expected: Per rule 400.2/429.2 (and the card family's reminder 'abilities that add resources can't be reacted to'), an activated Add ability finalizes and resolves immediately without creating a respondable chain item — Energy Conduit (ogn-098-298) in the same game did exactly that (energy credited instantly, no chain)
findings.observed: Activating Platewyrm Egg's ability created chain item {type:'conditional', condition:while-empowered, then add-resource 2, else add-resource 1} and required passChainPriority (p1, and p2 when driven) before the energy was added; opponents therefore get a window to respond. Likely the immediate-resolve check doesn't recognise add-resource nested inside a conditional.
findings.reason: The parser (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/activated.ts:298-315) emits Platewyrm Egg's ability effect as {type:'conditional', condition:{type:'while-empowered'}, then:add-resource, else:add-resource}. The engine's immediate-resolve gate at riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/chain/activate-ability.ts:1399-1400 only checks the TOP-LEVEL effect type (`effectType === "add-resource" || effectType === "add"`); a 'conditional' wrapper fails that check and falls through to addToChain at line 1429, creating a respondable chain item. Same top-level-only check at line 533 (mid-payment usability). This violates rule 429.2 (activated Add abilities resolve as soon as finalized; priority does not pass).

findings.what: "When you play me or I attack, you may pay [2] to Stun a unit" never triggers
findings.expected: On playing Kennen (from hand or from face-down via Hidden) and on Kennen attacking, an optional prompt/chain item to pay 2 energy and stun a chosen unit
findings.observed: Played Kennen to base (energy 20->17): no chain item, no pendingChoice, log only 'played Kennen'. Revealed a hidden Kennen onto a battlefield: no trigger. Moved Kennen to enemy-occupied battlefield (combat showdown, combatRole=attacker): no trigger. Runtime parse of the card (getCardRegistry) yields only [Hidden keyword, static modify-might] — the triggered ability is dropped entirely.
findings.reason: Reproduced via runtime parse: getCardRegistry().get("ven-135-166").abilities yields only [{keyword:"Hidden"},{static modify-might}] — the "When you play me or I attack, you may pay [2] to [Stun] a unit" line is dropped. Root cause: /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/trigger-patterns.ts has no pattern for the compound trigger "When you play me or I attack," (it has "When I attack," at line 44, "When I attack or defend," at line 203, "When you play me or when I hold," at line 294, and the Jayce compound at line 438, but not play-self-or-attack). parseAbilities("When you play me or I attack, [Stun] a unit.") returns {success:false,"Could not parse ability text"}, whereas "When I attack, you may pay [2] to [Stun] a unit." and "When you play me, you may pay [2] ..." each parse fine into optional triggered abilities with pay-cost condition — so only the compound trigger prefix is unsupported. The card is loaded from data/sets/ven.json (abilities:[null,null] placeholder, re-parsed at load by data/enrich-cards.ts:30 enrichCard), with no hand-authored override, so the multi-line parser silently omits the unparseable line and no play-self/attack trigger ever exists for the engine to fire.

findings.what: "While there's a stunned enemy unit here, I have +2 Might" does not apply
findings.expected: With a stunned enemy Pouty Poro at the same battlefield, Kennen should be 4 Might (and win combat vs a 3-Might stunned defender)
findings.observed: Enemy Pouty Poro at Altar to Unity had meta.stunned=true/__flags.stunned=true; Kennen at same battlefield stayed might 2 with no staticMightBonus, UI showed no might badge; after buffing Poro to 3 Might and resolveFullCombat, Poro survived and Kennen was recalled to base (i.e. Kennen dealt 2, not 4). Parsed static is {modify-might +2, target:{unit, controller:enemy, location:here, filter:stunned}} — i.e. it targets stunned enemy units instead of being a conditional self-buff (and the 'stunned' filter reads top-level meta rather than __flags).
findings.reason: Reproduced via getCardRegistry().get("ven-135-166"): parsed abilities are [keyword Hidden, static {modify-might +2, target:{unit, controller:enemy, location:here, filter:stunned}}] — an aura on stunned enemy units, not a conditional self-buff, so Kennen never gains +2 (and the pay-[2]-to-Stun trigger is dropped entirely). Root cause: packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/normalize.ts:21 stripReminders' /_?\s*\([^)]*\)\s*_?/ eats the reminder "(It doesn't deal combat damage this turn.)" together with the following newline, gluing the lines into "...to Stun a unit.While there's a stunned enemy unit here, I have +2 :rb_might:."; splitOnAbilityBoundaries doesn't split it, triggered parse fails, and packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/parsers/static-parser.ts:642-648 matches `^(.+?)\s+have\s+\+(\d+)` with subject "When you play me ... unit.While there's a stunned enemy unit here, I" — the guard at :647 only exempts subjects that START with While/If, so parseGrantTarget(subject) yields {enemy, here, stunned}. Parsing the third line alone correctly hits the conditional self-might branch at static-parser.ts:772-795. (Minor: the sub-claim that the 'stunned' filter ignores __flags is not accurate — riftbound-engine/src/abilities/target-resolver.ts:659-664 reads both — but the primary misparse is real.)

findings.what: 'When you play me ... you may ready something besides me that's exhausted' resolves as a no-op
findings.expected: After accepting the opt-in, a target prompt for an exhausted permanent/rune other than Jayce (Pouty Poro was exhausted in base) and the chosen target becomes ready
findings.observed: Trigger went on chain with effect {type:'raw', text:'ready something besides me that's exhausted.'}; opt-in pendingChoice appeared and was accepted, but no target prompt followed and Pouty Poro stayed exhausted=true. Effect is unparsed/unimplemented (ven.json parseSuccess:false, abilities:[])
findings.reason: parseAbilities on Jayce's rulesText (invoked at packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/enrich-cards.ts:30) produces a triggered ability (event play-self-or-play-gear, optional:true) whose effect is {type:'raw', text:"ready something besides me that's exhausted."} — the effect clause is unparsed (fallback at packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/triggers.ts:230). In the engine, executeEffect (packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts:172-184) does EFFECT_HANDLERS[effect.type]; there is no 'raw' handler anywhere under abilities/, so it hits the '// default: no-op' branch at line 183. Hence opt-in resolves with no target prompt and nothing is readied. No TS card override exists for ven-068a-166 (only ven.json, parseSuccess:false, abilities:[]).

findings.what: 'the first time you play a non-token gear each turn' trigger never fires
findings.expected: With Jayce in base, playing Seal of Discord (first non-token gear this turn) puts Jayce's ready trigger on the chain / opt-in prompt
findings.observed: playGear resolved, Seal of Discord entered base, chain=null and pendingChoice=null; no Jayce trigger
findings.reason: Jayce (ven-068a-166) has no hand-authored ability; runtime parse (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/trigger-patterns.ts:435-438) yields trigger {event:"play-self-or-play-gear", on:"self"} with a raw effect. In riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-matcher.ts:346-350, the on:"self" branch rejects any event whose cardId != the ability holder's id. play-gear.ts:269 fires {type:"play-card", cardId:<gear>, cardType:"gear"}, so the "play-gear" half of the compound matches the event type (line 321-323) but is then rejected because event.cardId (Seal of Discord) !== Jayce's id. Verified by calling findMatchingTriggers directly: play-card/gear event with Jayce in base returns [] while play-self returns the match. So the gear-play trigger can never fire (additionally the effect is type:"raw", so even the play-self half would do nothing useful).

findings.what: Look-at-top-5 prompt only displays the eligible units, not all 5 looked-at cards
findings.expected: 'Look at the top 5 cards of your Main Deck' — player sees all 5 revealed cards (Flame Chompers, Immortal Phoenix, Doran's Ring, Seal of Discord, Detonate) with only units selectable
findings.observed: Engine pendingChoice.revealed listed all 5 ids, but the 'Choose a card to play' modal rendered only Flame Chompers and Immortal Phoenix plus 'No'; the 3 non-unit cards were never shown to the player
findings.reason: renderPendingChoiceModal (modals.js:93-107) builds the card row solely from availableMoves resolvePendingChoice entries with params.pickedCardId (i.e. only the filter-eligible units) and never reads pending.revealed, so the blocking 'Choose a card to play' modal shows only Flame Chompers/Immortal Phoenix + 'No'. Caveat: the sidebar action list does render pending.revealed thumbnails (render/actions.js:223-232), but while the modal is up they sit beneath the fixed full-viewport 70%-opaque #choiceOverlay (gameplay.css:695-706, z-index 1500; not in 'targeting' mode since deck cards aren't on the board), in a 220px-max scroll panel — so 'never shown' is slightly overstated, but the modal defect is real.

findings.what: 'When I attack, choose an enemy unit here' target prompt offers every unit on the board, including friendly units, units in base, and Riven herself
findings.expected: choose-target options limited to enemy units at the battlefield Riven is attacking (here: Mega-Mech and Playful Phantom only)
findings.observed: pendingChoice choose-target options = [player-1 Mystic Poro (friendly, in base), player-2 Mega-Mech, player-2 Playful Phantom, player-1 Riven, Shattered (self)]; UI 'Choose a target' modal showed all four. Server /api/cards/ven-041-166 shows the parsed triggered ability target is just {type:'unit'} with no controller:'enemy' / location:'here' restriction
findings.reason: Parser reproduces the report: parseAbilities on Riven, Shattered's text yields the triggered ability's damage effect with target {type:"unit"} only (ran the parser via bun). Root cause: packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/triggers.ts:68-71 strips the "Choose (a|an) (friendly|enemy)? unit (here|there|at a battlefield)." preamble from triggered-ability effect text and discards it (replace with ""), unlike spells.ts:180-194/216 which captures the preamble via CHOOSE_PREAMBLE_RE and bindChosenTarget()s it onto the "it" reference. The remaining "Deal 2 to it for each Equipment attached to me" hits effects-damage.ts:78-91 where parseCardTarget("it") produces an unrestricted {type:"unit"}, so the enemy/here restriction is lost and the engine offers every unit on board (friendly, in base, self).

findings.what: 'As you play this, name a tag' clause not implemented
findings.expected: Playing The List should prompt the player to name a tag (pendingChoice / prompt) and record it on the card
findings.observed: playGear resolved straight to base with no pendingChoice, no prompt in UI, and no named-tag stored in card meta; parseAbilities() output for this rulesText contains only the [Exhaust] activated ability — the name-a-tag clause is dropped
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/the-list.ts:4-15 has no `abilities` field, only rulesText. Running parseAbilities() on that rulesText yields exactly one ability — the [Exhaust] activated modify-might with target filter {tag:"named"} (parser/impl/effects-might.ts:120-139); the "As you play this, name a tag" sentence produces nothing (no parser rule matches "name a tag" — the only "As you play this" handlers are additional-cost patterns in spells.ts:74/155, replacement.ts:25, effects-conditional.ts:57). Engine side: there is a name-card effect (abilities/effects/name-card.ts, namedCard meta) but no name-tag equivalent; grep for namedTag/name-tag in riftbound-engine/src, server.ts, and public/js/gameplay returns nothing. target-resolver.ts:737-739 treats filter.tag "named" as a literal tag string via tags.includes("named"), so no named tag is ever prompted for or stored.

findings.what: [Exhaust] ability cannot be activated
findings.expected: With The List ready on board and a Poro-tagged unit (Pouty Poro) in play, activateAbility should be enumerated and give the unit -2 Might this turn
findings.observed: pw moves lists no activateAbility for The List; direct executeMove/REST activateAbility returns CONDITION_FAILED (target filter {tag:'named'} never matches because no tag can be named). Manually labelCard='Poro' did not help either.
findings.reason: Parser (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-might.ts:121-139) emits The List's exhaust effect with target filter { tag: "named" } as a literal placeholder. The engine's filter matcher (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/target-resolver.ts:737-739) compares filter.tag literally against the card definition's tags array (`tags?.includes(filter.tag)`), so it looks for a unit whose printed tag is the string "named" — never true for Pouty Poro (tag "Poro"). There is no engine support for "As you play this, name a tag": grep for 'name a tag'/'named' in riftbound-engine/src finds nothing, and labelCard (game-definition/moves/card-actions.ts:88-95) only writes meta.label, which target-resolver never consults for tag filters. Hence no legal target exists, activateAbility is not enumerated, and direct execution fails the target condition.

findings.what: 'Discard a gear' cost is not enforced or paid
findings.expected: Ability should be unactivatable with no gear in hand; when activated it should require choosing/discarding a gear from hand (like Punching Poro's Empower which enumerates discardId)
findings.observed: activateAbility was offered and accepted with zero gear in hand; with Spirit's Refuge (gear) in hand, activation still discarded nothing (gear stayed in hand, trash unchanged, no discard prompt, no discardId param enumerated)
findings.reason: Sky Cruiser's runtime ability cost (verified via getAllCards) is `{discard:{amount:1,cardType:"gear"}, energy:1, exhaust:true}` — the parser emits an object shape at packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/activated.ts:227. The engine only handles `cost.discard` as a number: activate-ability.ts:715-716 (condition) and :1068-1071 (enumerator) do `discardCost && discardCost > 0`, which is false for an object, so no hand-size/gear gating and no discardId enumeration; there is also no cardType filter anywhere. In the reducer (activate-ability.ts:1272-1291 then 1324-1327) energy/exhaust are paid, then `if (cost.discard) { if (!discardId) return; }` early-returns without trashing anything. Matches observed: activatable with no gear, no discard prompt, gear stays in hand.

findings.what: Effect 'Deal 4 to a unit at a battlefield' never happens
findings.expected: Target Playful Phantom (5 might, at battlefield) should take 4 damage after ability resolves
findings.observed: After activateAbility {targets:[Phantom]}: energy -1 and Sky Cruiser exhausted (costs taken) but no chain item was created, no pendingChoice, and Phantom meta.damage stayed 0 (twice). Control: Hextech Ray on the same Phantom correctly set damage=3, so damage tracking works — the ability's effect is simply dropped
findings.reason: Sky Cruiser (ven-060-166) has no hand-authored abilities in ven.json; enrichCard re-parses rulesText at runtime into an activated ability with cost `{discard: {amount: 1, cardType: "gear"}, energy: 1, exhaust: true}` (verified by dumping getCardRegistry().get("ven-060-166")). The discard cost is an OBJECT, but activate-ability.ts only handles a numeric discard cost: condition (line 715-716) and enumerator (line 1068-1071) do `cost.discard as number; if (discardCost && discardCost > 0)` — `{...} > 0` is false, so no hand check runs and no `discardId` is enumerated/required. The reducer then pays energy (line 1272 deductAbilityCost) and sets exhausted (line 1290-1291) BEFORE reaching line 1324-1327: `if (cost.discard) { if (!discardId) { return; } }` — the object is truthy, discardId is undefined, so the reducer returns early after costs are taken and before addToChain (line 1429). Result: energy -1, host exhausted, no chain item, no pendingChoice, no damage — exactly the observed behavior.

findings.what: [Empower] — Kill a friendly unit activated ability is not offered/does nothing
findings.expected: With Escaped Grayback (not Empowered) in base and another friendly unit (Flame Chompers) in base, `pw moves` should list an activateAbility for Grayback whose cost kills a friendly unit and whose effect sets Grayback meta.empowered=true (then +2 Might applies).
findings.observed: No activateAbility move enumerated for Grayback at all (moves = endTurn/concede/rune moves only); calling executeMove('activateAbility',{cardId:Grayback,abilityIndex:0}) directly was a no-op (Flame Chompers still alive, no chain item, no empowered flag). Parser output for this rulesText contains only the while-empowered static (+2 might) — the `[Empower] — Kill a friendly unit` line is dropped because the [Empower] keyword-cost regex in riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/activated.ts only accepts energy/rune/exhaust costs, not a 'Kill a friendly unit' cost.
findings.reason: Verified via getAllCards(): ven-124-166 (Escaped Grayback) resolves to a single ability — the static {condition: while-empowered, effect: modify-might +2}. The "[Empower] — Kill a friendly unit" line is dropped. Root cause at /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/activated.ts:53-55 — the [Empower] keyword-cost regex only accepts :rb_energy_N:/:rb_rune_X:/:rb_exhaust: cost tokens, so a "Kill a friendly unit" cost never matches and no activated ability (cost: kill friendly unit, effect: empower self) is emitted. ven.json:3806-3808 has abilities:[null] and there is no hand-written src/cards override for this card, so the engine has no activated ability to enumerate or execute.

findings.what: 'When you play me from face down, you may empower something here' resolves as a no-op
findings.expected: After accepting the opt-in, a target prompt restricted to units/gear at the battlefield where Tornado Warrior was revealed (Recruit token or itself), chosen target gets meta.empowered=true, and a delayed disempower at end of turn.
findings.observed: Trigger fired correctly on play-from-hidden (chain item triggerEvent type 'play-from-hidden', optional opt-in pendingChoice shown). Accepting it (resolvePendingChoice accept:true) produced no target prompt and no state change: neither Tornado Warrior nor the Recruit token at that battlefield got meta.empowered; log only says 'resolve pending choice'. Chain effect is {type:'raw', text:'empower something here. Disempower it at end of turn.'} — parser leaves the effect unparsed so the engine has nothing to execute.
findings.reason: Ran the parser on Tornado Warrior's rulesText: the second ability parses as triggered/optional with trigger play-from-hidden, but effect = {type:"raw", text:"empower something here. Disempower it at end of turn."}. Cause: parseEmpowerEffect regex at packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-resources.ts:193 accepts "something" / "something else" but not "something here", and there is no handling for the trailing "Disempower it at end of turn." clause, so the effect falls through to raw. Engine executeEffect (packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts:172-184) has no handler for "raw" and hits the no-op branch — no target prompt, no meta.empowered, no delayed disempower.

findings.what: [Level 6] gate on 'When you play me, draw 1' is ignored
findings.expected: With player XP = 0 (< 6), playing Wuju Apprentice should not draw a card (effect only applies while you have 6+ XP).
findings.observed: At xp=0 the play-self trigger was put on the chain with effect {draw 1} and no condition, and on resolution hand went 5->6 (drew Tideturner). Parser emits condition {type:'while-level',threshold:6} on the triggered ability, but trigger-runner's triggered-ability condition evaluator has no 'while-level' case and falls through to permissive true (while-level is only handled for static/activated abilities and play cost).
findings.reason: Parser (packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/gated.ts) emits the Wuju Apprentice play-self triggered ability with condition {type:'while-level',threshold:6} (verified by running parseAbilities on the card's rulesText). The triggered-ability gate evaluateTriggerCondition in packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-runner.ts:289-521 handles legion, paid-additional-cost, excess-damage-assigned, played-power-cost, while-empowered, while-at-battlefield, fewer-runes-than-opponent, control, alone-in-combat, while-alone, exists-here, and, has-at-least — there is no 'while-level' branch, so it falls through to `return true` at trigger-runner.ts:520. grep confirms 'while-level' is only evaluated in static-abilities.ts:357, play/cost.ts:202, and activate-ability.ts:542/929. Hence at XP 0 the [Level 6] play trigger is put on the chain unconditionally and draws 1.
